record.paper_title: Open problems on structure of positively curved projective varieties
record.context_brief: Structure theorem for compact Kähler manifolds
record.original_question: Can the smooth-projective structure theorem for varieties with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature be extended to compact Kähler manifolds? In concrete terms, should such a compact Kähler manifold admit a locally trivial MRC fibration φ: X → Y to a flat base Y, with rationally connected fiber F; after a finite étale cover A → Y by an abelian variety, should the pullback X* = A ×_Y X have a locally trivial Albanese map to A; should the universal cover split as ℂ^m × F; and should the fundamental group be an extension of a finite group by a free abelian group?

evidence.quote: The morphism φ : X → Y is a locally trivial morphism.
The image Y is a smooth projective variety with a flat metric.
The fiber F is a rationally connected manifold. In particular, the morphism φ : X → Y is an MRC fibration of X.
We obtain an isomorphism Xuniv ∼= Cm × F, where Xuniv is the universal cover of X, and F is the rationally connected fiber of φ.
In particular, the fundamental group of X is an extension of a finite group by Z⊕2m.
It is an attractive problem to generalize the above structure theorem to compact Kähler manifolds. Problem 3.5. — Can we generalize Theorem 3.4 to compact Kähler manifolds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a compact connected Kähler manifold whose holomorphic sectional curvature is semi-positive (i.e. H(v) ≥ 0 for every nonzero holomorphic tangent vector v). Recall:

• A maximal rationally connected (MRC) fibration of X is an almost-holomorphic dominant meromorphic map φ : X ⇢ Y whose general fiber is rationally connected and maximal with this property.
• A surjective holomorphic map φ : X → Y between complex manifolds is called locally trivial if, locally on Y in the Euclidean topology, φ is biholomorphic to a projection Y × F → Y for a fixed fiber F.
• A Kähler metric on Y is called flat if its holomorphic sectional curvature (equivalently its full curvature tensor for a Kähler metric of constant zero sectional curvature) vanishes identically.

Prove or disprove that every such X enjoys all four of the following properties simultaneously:

(1) The MRC fibration of X is represented by a holomorphic locally trivial fibration φ : X → Y onto a smooth compact Kähler manifold Y carrying a flat Kähler metric, with rationally connected fiber F.

(2) There exists a finite étale cover A → Y where A is a complex torus (an abelian variety in the projective case) such that the base-changed family X* := A ×_Y X → A is the Albanese map of X*, and this Albanese map is locally trivial.

(3) The universal cover of X is biholomorphic to ℂ^m × F, where m = dim Y and F is the rationally connected fiber of φ.

(4) The fundamental group π_1(X) fits into a short exact sequence
  1 → ℤ^{2m} → π_1(X) → G → 1
with G a finite group; equivalently, π_1(X) is an extension of a finite group by a free abelian group of rank 2m.
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous structure theorem in the smooth projective case is established (work of Matsumura and others). The Kähler extension is generally regarded as open: partial results exist in low dimensions (Kähler surfaces and certain 3-folds with nonnegative holomorphic sectional curvature), and the quasi-positive Kähler case has been shown to imply projectivity and rational connectedness. No source verifies the full four-part Kähler structure theorem in arbitrary dimension.

status_evidence.title: Compact Kähler manifolds with quasi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature (Shiyu Zhang)
status_evidence.snippet: shows compact Kähler manifolds with quasi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature are projective and rationally connected, answering a question of Yang and Matsumura
status_evidence.claim: partial progress on the Kähler version; full structure theorem not stated as proved

status_evidence.title: Structure of compact Kähler manifolds (arXiv 2311.18779)
status_evidence.snippet: Matsumura's structure theorem applies to projective manifolds; extensions to the Kähler setting are subject of current research
status_evidence.claim: Kähler generalization is an active open direction
